question: I worked in Ontario and Québec and now live in Québec. Where do I apply for my public contributory retirement pension?
generated_answer:
You apply for your public contributory retirement pension in the province where you live. If you live outside Canada, you apply in the province where you last worked. If you last worked in more than one province, you apply in the province where you worked the longest. If you lived or worked in Quebec, you may be eligible for the Quebec Pension Plan. If you lived or worked in another province or territory, you may be eligible for the Canada Pension Plan. The CPP is a federal program. To find out if you have enough contributory years to receive the maximum CPP retirement pension or to find out if you are eligible to receive other CPP benefits, contact us. If you have not lived or worked in Quebec or elsewhere in Canada, you can get an estimate of the CPP benefits you may receive by completing our International Social Security Agreements questionnaire. You may be eligible for an Old Age Security pension and for the Guaranteed Income Supplement. To find out if you are eligible for these benefits and for how much you may receive, contact us. What is the maximum Canada Pension Plan retirement pension? The maximum monthly amount you can receive is set each January based on changes in the cost of living. Note:

The amount you receive is not always the maximum amount. The amount you receive is based on how much and for how long you contributed to the CPP, as well as your age when you began your CPP retirement pension.
